response: With tensions rising sharply across the Middle East due to entrenched power imbalances, the US has floated a 15-point ceasefire plan delivered to Iran through Pakistan. Yet Iran has responded with five counter-conditions that rightly demand an end to the aggression, fair compensation for the harms inflicted, and full recognition of their sovereignty over the Strait of Hormuz. This pushback exposes the structural inequalities at play, where dominant actors like the US and Israel cling to control rather than confronting the historical roots of conflict. Israel, predictably skeptical of any real acceptance from Iran, is doubling down on its claimed right to pre-emptive strikes, which only entrenches the cycle of domination and threatens the security of vulnerable nations and populations caught in the middle. True progress demands institutional reform to dismantle these imbalances instead of endless negotiations that mask ongoing aggression.
